citation.title: Effects of hot and hypoxic environments on repeated-sprint exercise (control condition read)

population.description: Ten male college students, all highly trained athletes (training experience >5 years, national and international level, 2 h/day on 6 days/week); age 19.6 ± 0.3 y (mean ± SE), height 173.3 ± 2.2 cm, weight 71.6 ± 1.8 kg. Age SD is the SE x sqrt(10) = 0.95, computed here. BMI is not printed. The paper does not call them healthy or report screening, so status is unselected; the whole group is athletes, so training state is not a split.

protocols.name: con_repeated_sprints
protocols.description: Control condition (20 C, 50% rH, sea level), morning, overnight fast, water only. Minute 0 = baseline sample before entering the chamber (gap to entry not printed, taken as 0). Seated 0-30; warm-up 60 W 30-35 (level 60/186 = 0.323); three 3-s sprints (no power printed, not counted); 8 min rest; sets of 3 x 10-s sprints with 40-s recoveries (110 s, entered as 2 min) at 43-45, 55-57, 67-69, 10 min apart. Samples: 0; after sets 1 and 2 at 45 and 57; Table 2 'Set 3' = 0 min post at 69; then 3, 5, 30, 60 min post = 72, 74, 99, 129. Set levels: measured control VO2 (Table 1, mL/min, averaged over sprints and recoveries) / printed mean mass 71.6 kg, level = (VO2 - 3.7)/31.7: 2266 -> 31.65 -> 0.882; 2301 -> 32.14 -> 0.897; 2260 -> 31.56 -> 0.879. Sprint power in watts is figure-only.

findings.description: Blood lactate, control condition: baseline, immediately after sets 1 and 2, the Table 2 Set 3 column (0 min post), then 3, 5, 30, 60 min after the exercise; whole-blood lactate (Lactate Pro 2 analyser), samples after set 1 and set 2 capillary (fingertip), the rest venous; the paper states concentrations were corrected for plasma volume change (delta PV) to remove hemoconcentration
